headline: Photosynthesis converts sunlight into food—plants capture light and build themselves from air and water
universal_truth: Energy must be captured before it can be used; all value starts with some form of harvest
fun_facts: Plants produce all the oxygen you breathe as a byproduct of photosynthesis
A single tree can absorb about 48 pounds of carbon dioxide per year
Chlorophyll reflects green light, which is why plants appear green—they use red and blue light
discussion_questions: What 'sunlight' do you capture and convert into value?
Where does your energy ultimately come from?
What inputs do you transform into outputs?

hook.script: Plants are solar-powered factories. They capture photons from the sun, pull carbon dioxide from air, draw water from soil, and build themselves—sugar, cellulose, wood. From light and air, they create matter. This is photosynthesis: the foundation of almost all life.

cliff.script: All food energy on Earth traces back to photosynthesis. Plants capture sunlight; everything else just transfers that captured energy. What does this teach us about value creation?
cliff.prompt: What does photosynthesis teach about value?

options.text: Value must first be captured from some source—before you can transform or transfer energy, someone or something must harvest it from the environment
options.response: Yes. Plants are primary producers—they capture energy that then flows through all life. Understanding the source of value shows where prosperity begins.
They're food, but more fundamentally they're energy capturers—the foundation everything else depends on...

fact1.title: Light to Matter
fact1.script: Photosynthesis uses light energy to break water molecules, releasing oxygen. The hydrogen combines with carbon dioxide to form glucose—sugar. Light becomes matter. The tree's wood was once sunlight and air.

fact2.title: Primary Production
fact2.script: Plants are primary producers—they create food from non-food. Everything else is secondary: eating plants, eating plant-eaters, decomposing remains. All energy traces back to photosynthetic capture.

fact3.title: Your Energy Source
fact3.script: You run on captured sunlight too—just filtered through food chains. The energy in your breakfast was sunlight, captured by plants, perhaps eaten by animals, now powering your thoughts. You're solar-powered.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Energy must be captured before it can be used. All value starts with some form of harvest. Know where your energy comes from.

outro.script: That's Day 241. Tomorrow, we'll explore how bodies make energy—metabolism. Until then, trace your food back to its sunlight source.

growTrack.title: Energy Tracing - Where Does Yours Come From?
growTrack.learning_objective: Trace energy sources to their origins
growTrack.activity: Pick something you consumed today—food, fuel, electricity. Trace it back: where did that energy originally come from? Most paths lead to sunlight captured by plants. Understanding energy sources reveals hidden dependencies.
